correction.text: 'found primarily on the Deccan Plateau of southern India', 'concentrated in the modern states of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana', 'the river valleys of the Tungabhadra, Krishna, and Hagari'; the Bellary (Kupgal, Sanganakallu), Raichur, Kalaburagi (Budihal) and Kurnool country, with discs on the Hagari valley near Anantapur (Palavoy) and on Hallur

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). 'dated to the Neolithic period, approximately 3200 to 1200 BC'; 'Over 200 sites were recorded by Robert Foote'. The page gives no area; the shape resolves to about 114,000 km2 and is a union of discs around the named districts, not a boundary.

ledger.note: c. 3200 BCE: the ashmound Neolithic of the southern Deccan begins. 'these man-made accumulations of fossilised ash have been dated to the Neolithic period, approximately 3200 to 1200 BC'; 'Found primarily on the Deccan Plateau of southern India'. The year is the page's; the country is my reading of the named states, rivers and districts.

ledger.note: c. 1200 BCE: the Neolithic ashmound tradition ends. 'approximately 3200 to 1200 BC'; 'while the ashmounds were initiated during the Neolithic, their use continued into the Iron Age' (upper layers at Palavoy show 'iron objects and Iron Age ceramics'). The Iron Age megalithic culture of the south has no dossier here.

certainty.note: A tradition known from over 200 ashmound sites; the page gives states, river valleys and districts, not frontiers.

sources.title: Neolithic ashmounds
sources.note: Dates approximately 3200-1200 BC, Deccan Plateau, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, Tungabhadra, Krishna and Hagari valleys, Bellary and Kalaburagi districts, over 200 sites, Iron Age continuation.

notes: Type culture; no Cliopatria row; the page has no infobox, no area, no phases and no 'preceded/followed by'. It is a page about ashmound sites, used here as the only Wikipedia page on the southern Neolithic; the name is mine. Shape: discs on Ballari (120 km), Raichur (110), Kalaburagi (80), Kurnool (110), the Hagari valley near Anantapur (80 km at 77.6E 14.7N, Palavoy) and Hallur (60 km at 75.4E 14.8N); Anantapur, Hallur, Utnur and Valasai (Tamil Nadu) are not gazetteer places, and Valasai is left out. The Tungabhadra-Krishna river bands would give 180-220,000 km2 including the Maharashtra Krishna valley, which the page does not place. The 'preceded/followed by' relation to the Iron Age megalithic culture is the page's only link; that culture (and the Southern chiefdoms of the scope) need a dossier from a page with an extent.
